content.overview: A Producer Company shall not alter the conditions in its memorandum except in the cases, by the mode and to the extent for which express provision is made in the Act. It may, by special resolution not inconsistent with section 378B, alter its objects. The amended memorandum and a certified copy of the special resolution must be filed with the Registrar within thirty days. Change of registered office from one State to another requires Central Government approval and dual-Registrar filing.
content.glance: Objects may be altered by special resolution consistent with s. 378B; inter-State registered-office change needs Central Government approval.
content.study: Section 378H restricts alteration of the memorandum to the modes and extent expressly provided. Objects may be altered by special resolution so long as the new objects remain within section 378B. Filing with the Registrar (and, on inter-State office transfer, with both Registrars) is mandatory within thirty days. Alteration of the place of the registered office from one State to another takes effect only on Central Government approval.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Memorandum conditions may be altered only as expressly permitted; objects may be altered by special resolution consistent with s. 378B; inter-State office change needs Central Government approval.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378H
examples.body: A special resolution that replaces one s. 378B object with another s. 378B object, followed by timely Registrar filing, is a valid amendment under s. 378H(2).

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378H?
hypotheticals.analysis: It confines memorandum alterations to express statutory modes, requires special resolution for objects changes consistent with s. 378B, and subjects inter-State office moves to Central Government approval.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming objects may be altered to any commercial purpose.
misconceptions.correction: The special resolution must keep the objects within the list in s. 378B.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the proposed alteration. II. Check the statutory mode, objects consistency and filing/approval requirements. III. Conclude.
